sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner/respondent No.1 and on perusal of the writ petition papers, I am of the view that petitioner/respondent No.1 has not made out any ground NC: 2023:KHC:40841 to interfere with impugned order.
Further, impugned order is neither perverse nor suffers from any material irregularity so as to warrant interference under Article 227 of Constitution of India.

5. Petitioner/respondent No.1 filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the accidental injuries suffered in a road traffic accident that took place on 14.12.2019 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-21-S-7357 and car bearing registration No.KA-20-Z-3239.
Petitioner/respondent No.1 is made respondent alleging that he is the owner of the car which was involved in the accident.
It is the case of the petitioner/respondent No.1 that as on the date of accident i.e., on 14.12.2019, petitioner/respondent No.1 had sold the car on 15.05.2019 to the proposed respondent No.3.
Since petitioner/respondent No.1 had sold the offending vehicle to proposed respondent No.3, respondent No.3 - purchaser would be proper and necessary party to the claim petition.

It is to be noticed that RC of the vehicle would determine the ownership of the vehicle and RC of the vehicle in question was standing in the name of the petitioner as on the date of accident i.e.,
14.12.2019.
It is for the petitioner/respondent No.1 to prove that he had sold the offending vehicle as on the date of accident and he is not the owner of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Thereafter burden is on the claimant to implead the owner as on the date of accident or to take further steps in the matter.
In the light of the above, I do not find any error in the order passed by Tribunal.
Accordingly, writ petition stands rejected.
